definition_en: a company or person that provides goods or services to another business
core_image: 仓库门口，一箱箱货物交到采购方手里
scene: 工厂的装配线眼看要停，采购经理一遍遍催促供货方发货。The factory called every supplier to confirm the delivery date.
sceneCN: 这里 supplier 是「供应商」（第 1 个义项：向其他企业提供货物的一方）；句意：工厂给每一位供应商打电话确认交货日期。

derivatives.zh: 供应；提供，由拉丁语 supplere（补足）经古法语进入英语
供应品；物资，supply 的复数名词形式
供给侧的，经济学中描述生产一端的复合形容词

senses.title: A company that provides goods
senses.definition: a business that hands over goods to another business or to customers
senses.definitionCN: 向其他企业或顾客交付货物的企业
senses.example: The hospital buys gloves from a local supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院从本地供应商那里采购手套。
senses.why: The suffix -er names the agent, and supply comes from Latin supplere, to fill up, so the supplier is the one who fills another firm gap.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 表示施事者，而 supply 来自拉丁语 supplere（补足），所以供应商就是替另一家企业补上缺口的那一方。

senses.title: The supplying party in a contract
senses.definition: the party named in a contract who must deliver goods or services to the other party
senses.definitionCN: 合同中具名、负有向另一方交付货物或服务义务的一方
senses.example: Under clause four, the supplier bears the transport risk.
senses.exampleCN: 根据第四条，供货方承担运输风险。
senses.why: Legal drafting turns the trading role into a defined party with duties, so the everyday vendor becomes a named supplier.
senses.whyCN: 法律起草把这个交易角色变成负有义务的具名当事方，于是日常的卖货人就成为合同中的供货方。

senses.title: A source of a resource or quality
senses.definition: a person, place, or thing that provides something needed, such as ideas, labour, or talent
senses.definitionCN: 提供所需之物的人、地方或事物，如想法、劳动力或人才
senses.example: The city is a major supplier of engineering talent.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市是工程人才的重要来源。
senses.why: The agent suffix lets the word move from goods to anything provided, so a city can supply talent just as a firm supplies parts.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀让这个词从货物扩展到任何被提供的东西，所以城市能提供人才，正如企业提供零件。

intro.en: Supplier joins the Latin verb supplere, to fill up, with the English agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: supplier 由拉丁语动词 supplere（补足）加英语施事后缀 -er 构成。

items.en: Supplere is built from sub, under, and plere, to fill.
items.cn: supplere 由 sub（在下）与 plere（填满）构成。

items.en: Supplementum names the thing that fills a gap.
items.cn: supplementum 指用来补上缺口的东西。

items.en: Supplier means to fill up or provide in Old French.
items.cn: 古法语 supplier 意为补足或提供。

items.en: English supply first means to fill a need.
items.cn: 英语 supply 最初意为补足所需。

items.en: The agent suffix -er forms supplier, the one who supplies.
items.cn: 施事后缀 -er 构成 supplier，指提供货物的一方。

items.en: Trade usage fixes supplier as the standard word for a vendor.
items.cn: 商业用法把 supplier 固定为「供应商」的标准说法。

note.en: Supplier sits inside the supply family, and its nearest trade neighbours are vendor, distributor, and provider.
note.cn: supplier 属于 supply 词族，最贴近的商业同类词是 vendor、distributor 与 provider。

entries.definition: goods and equipment provided for use
something added to complete a whole
a firm that sells goods, especially under a contract
a firm that passes products from makers to buyers
a person or firm that supplies something needed

normalIntro.en: Supplier is the filler of a gap: the suffix -er turns supply into the party who makes good what is missing.
normalIntro.cn: supplier 是补缺口的一方：后缀 -er 把 supply 变成把缺少的东西补上的人。

normal.en: Supply plus -er gives supplier, the one who supplies.
normal.cn: supply 加 -er 就是 supplier，提供货物的那一方。

normal.en: A supplier fills the gap between a factory and its raw materials.
normal.cn: 供应商填补工厂与原料之间的缺口。

normal.en: The agent ending -er turns y into i in supplier.
normal.cn: 施动词尾 -er 在 supplier 中把 y 变成 i。

normal.en: A sole supplier is the only vendor a buyer may use under the contract.
normal.cn: sole supplier 指合同下买方唯一可用的供应商。

normal.en: Compare vendor: vendor stresses the sale, supplier stresses the provision.
normal.cn: 对比 vendor：vendor 强调卖出，supplier 强调提供。

abstract.en: Picture a delivery van pulling up at a factory gate at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象清晨一辆货车停在工厂门口卸货。

abstract.en: Imagine a contract clause that pins the risk of transport on one named party.
abstract.cn: 想象一条合同条款把运输风险压在一个具名的当事方身上。

abstract.en: Think of a city that keeps sending engineers to the whole region.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市持续为整个地区输送工程师。

examples.en: The supplier agreed to replace the damaged parts within ten days.
examples.cn: 供应商同意在十天内更换受损零件。

examples.en: Small shops often buy stock from several suppliers.
examples.cn: 小店铺往往从几家供应商处进货。

examples.en: Late delivery by the supplier can trigger a penalty clause.
examples.cn: 供应商交货延迟可能触发违约罚则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒普莱尔」——谐音像「撒货上门的人」，把货撒到货架上就是供应商；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ plere（填满）→ supplere（补足）→ 古法语 supplier（补足、提供）→ 英语 supply（供应），再加 -er 成为 supplier：把对方缺的东西补上的那一方。

sensesIntro.en: Supplier starts as the trading firm that hands over goods, narrows in contracts to the party bound to deliver, and widens again to any source of a needed resource.
sensesIntro.cn: supplier 先指交货的贸易企业，在合同里收窄为负有交货义务的一方，又扩大为任何所需资源的来源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cart of goods filling the empty space at another firm door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一车货物填上另一家企业门口的缺口。

branches.en: The everyday firm that delivers goods.
branches.cn: 日常义项：交付货物的企业。

branches.en: The party named in a contract as the deliverer.
branches.cn: 合同义项：被列为交货方的当事人。

branches.en: Any source of a resource or quality.
branches.cn: 比喻义项：任何资源或特质的来源。

branches.en: Both senses name a deliverer of goods; trade usage stresses the market role, contract usage the legal duty.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指交货方，商业用法强调市场角色，合同用法强调法律义务。

branches.en: Both describe a providing role, one fixed by contract and one figurative.
branches.cn: 两者都描述提供者角色，一个由合同固定，一个是比喻。

intro.en: Supplier grows from the Latin verb supplere, to fill up, through English supply and the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: supplier 从拉丁语动词 supplere（补足）经英语 supply 与施动词尾 -er 发展而来。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplere means to fill up, from sub, under, and plere, to fill.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 supplere 意为补足，由 sub（在下）与 plere（填满）构成。

items.example: The prefix sub- appears as sup- before p.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 在 p 前写作 sup-。

items.example: Plere is the filling root.
items.exampleCN: plere 是表示「填满」的词根。

items.example: Supplere adds the prefix to the filling root.
items.exampleCN: supplere 把前缀加到「填满」词根上。

items.example: Supplementum names the filler itself.
items.exampleCN: supplementum 指补缺的那个东西。

items.example: Supply carries the verb sense into English.
items.exampleCN: supply 把动词义带入英语。

items.example: Supplies is the plural mass noun.
items.exampleCN: supplies 是复数物资名词。

items.example: The suffix -er turns verbs into agent nouns.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把动词变成施事名词。

items.example: Supplier is the agent noun of supply.
items.exampleCN: supplier 是 supply 的施事名词。

items.example: Supplement comes from supplementum.
items.exampleCN: supplement 来自 supplementum。

items.example: Supply-side describes a kind of economic policy.
items.exampleCN: supply-side 描述一种经济政策。

definition_en: money paid by a government to lower the cost of a good, service, or activity
core_image: 政府把一叠钞票垫在农户的账本下面
scene: 粮价太低，农户连化肥都买不起，政府决定按亩发放补助。The government offered a subsidy to every farm that switched to cleaner fuel.
sceneCN: 这里 subsidy 是「补贴」（第 1 个义项：政府为降低成本而支付的补助）；句意：政府向每一户改用清洁燃料的农场发放补贴。

derivatives.zh: 补贴；给……发补助，由 subsidy 加动词后缀 -ize 构成
获得补贴的，subsidize 的过去分词作形容词
补贴行为；补贴制度，由 subsidize 加 -ation 构成
子公司；附属机构，与 subsidy 同出拉丁语 subsidium，词义转向「后备、辅助」

senses.title: A government payment that lowers costs
senses.definition: money a government pays to a producer or consumer so that a good or service costs less
senses.definitionCN: 政府向生产者或消费者支付、使某项商品或服务更便宜的款项
senses.example: The subsidy keeps the price of bread low for poor households.
senses.exampleCN: 这项补贴让贫困家庭买得起面包。
senses.why: Latin subsidium meant troops kept in reserve, so a subsidy is money held ready to back a cause when it is needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 subsidium 指留在后方的后备部队，所以补贴就是备好、需要时用来支撑某项事业的钱。

senses.title: The sum of money paid out
senses.definition: the amount of money actually paid under a support scheme
senses.definitionCN: 在补助方案下实际支付的金额
senses.example: Each family receives a monthly subsidy for heating.
senses.exampleCN: 每户每月领取一笔取暖补贴。
senses.why: The scheme and the cash it pays share one word, a shift from the support itself to the money that supports.
senses.whyCN: 方案与它付出的钱共用一词，这是从「支持」本身转到「支撑所用的钱」。

senses.title: A hidden support that lowers real costs
senses.definition: a benefit such as a tax break or a cheap loan that works like a payment because it lowers the real cost
senses.definitionCN: 税收减免或低息贷款等好处，因降低实际成本而起到类似付款的作用
senses.example: A low-interest loan acts as a hidden subsidy for exporters.
senses.exampleCN: 低息贷款对出口商来说是一种隐性补贴。
senses.why: Economists widen the word to cover any measure that shifts costs away from the buyer, even when no cash is handed over.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把这个词扩大到任何把成本从买方身上移开的措施，即使并没有现金过手。

intro.en: Subsidy goes back to Latin subsidium, a body of troops held in reserve, and later any help or support.
intro.cn: subsidy 可追溯到拉丁语 subsidium，指留在后方的后备部队，后来泛指援助与支持。

items.en: Subsidium means troops kept in reserve behind the line.
items.cn: subsidium 指留在战线后方的后备部队。

items.en: The same noun also means help or support in general.
items.cn: 同一名词也泛指帮助与支援。

items.en: Subsidium comes to mean a grant of money from a ruler.
items.cn: 在中世纪拉丁语里，subsidium 转指君主拨给的款项。

items.en: Subsidie passes into Anglo-French as a money grant.
items.cn: subsidie 经盎格鲁法语传入，指拨付的款项。

items.en: Subsidy first names a tax granted to the Crown.
items.cn: 英语 subsidy 最初指议会批给王室的税款。

items.en: Modern economics narrows subsidy to state support for producers or consumers.
items.cn: 现代经济学把 subsidy 收窄为政府对生产者或消费者的支持。

note.en: Subsidy shares the reserve image with subsidize and subsidiary, and sits close to grant, allowance, and rebate.
note.cn: subsidy 与 subsidize、subsidiary 共享「后备」意象，并与 grant、allowance、rebate 意义相邻。

entries.definition: to pay a subsidy to a person or industry
a company controlled by a larger parent company
money given for a specific purpose, often without repayment
a regular sum paid to someone for a stated purpose
a partial refund of money already paid

normalIntro.en: Subsidy carries the idea of a reserve: something set aside behind the line to support the front.
normalIntro.cn: subsidy 带着「后备」的意味：留在后方、随时支撑前线的东西。

normal.en: Subsidium first meant troops held in reserve.
normal.cn: subsidium 最初指留在后方的后备部队。

normal.en: A subsidy is money kept ready to support a cause.
normal.cn: 补贴就是备好用来支撑某项事业的钱。

normal.en: Governments use a subsidy to lower a price without fixing it.
normal.cn: 政府用补贴压低价格，而不直接定价。

normal.en: Subsidize is the verb and subsidized the adjective.
normal.cn: subsidize 是动词，subsidized 是形容词。

normal.en: Compare grant: a grant funds a project, a subsidy lowers a cost.
normal.cn: 对比 grant：grant 资助项目，subsidy 降低成本。

abstract.en: Picture a reserve squad sitting on the bench, ready to join the game.
abstract.cn: 想象替补队员坐在场边，随时准备上场。

abstract.en: Imagine a wallet kept in a drawer for a day when the family needs it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只放在抽屉里的钱包，等家里需要时拿出来。

abstract.en: Think of a shop that quietly pays part of your bill at the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一家商店在收银台悄悄替你付掉一部分账单。

examples.en: The government pays a subsidy to farmers who plant cover crops.
examples.cn: 政府向种植覆盖作物的农户发放补贴。

examples.en: Without the subsidy, the bus service would have to raise fares.
examples.cn: 没有这笔补贴，公交服务就不得不涨价。

examples.en: The subsidy was cut after a review found the scheme wasteful.
examples.cn: 审查认定该方案浪费后，补贴被削减。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「萨布西迪」——谐音像「塞补助」，就是政府塞给企业的后备钱；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下、后方）+ sedere（坐）→ subsidium（坐在后方的后备部队、支援）→ 中世纪拉丁语「君主拨给的款项」→ 英语 subsidy（补贴）。

sensesIntro.en: Subsidy starts as a support scheme, then names the cash it pays, and finally widens to any benefit that lowers a real cost.
sensesIntro.cn: subsidy 先指一套支持方案，再指它付出的那笔钱，最后扩大到任何降低实际成本的好处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a reserve of money waiting behind the front line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一笔待在后方的备用钱。

branches.en: The support scheme that lowers prices.
An indirect benefit that works like cash.
branches.cn: 起到现金作用的间接好处。

branches.en: The scheme and its payment are two sides of one policy.
branches.cn: 方案与付款是同一项政策的两个侧面。

branches.en: Cash and hidden benefit both shift cost away from the buyer.
branches.cn: 现金与隐性好处都把成本从买方身上移开。

intro.en: Subsidy is built on the Latin verb sedere, to sit, with the prefix sub-, and it has produced a whole English family.
intro.cn: subsidy 建立在拉丁语动词 sedere（坐）与前缀 sub- 之上，并衍生出整族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin subsidium means a reserve or support, literally what sits behind the line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 subsidium 意为后备或支援，字面就是「坐在战线后面的东西」。

items.example: The prefix sub- gives the idea of placing something behind.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 表示把某物放在后面。

items.example: Sedere is the sitting root of the family.
items.exampleCN: sedere 是这个词族里表示「坐」的词根。

items.example: Subsidium is the direct source of subsidy.
items.exampleCN: subsidium 是 subsidy 的直接来源。

items.example: Subsidiarius leads to the English subsidiary.
items.exampleCN: subsidiarius 引出英语 subsidiary。

items.meaning: state money that lowers a cost
items.example: Subsidy keeps the noun sense of support.
items.exampleCN: subsidy 保留「支持」的名词含义。

items.example: The suffix -ize turns the noun into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 把这个名词变成动词。

items.example: The past participle works as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词在这里作形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ation names the process.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 表示过程。

items.example: Subsidiary keeps the auxiliary idea.
items.exampleCN: subsidiary 保留「辅助」的意思。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms verbs from nouns.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 把名词构成动词。

definition_en: the government agency that controls goods crossing a border, or the tax it collects on them
core_image: 关口前排着货柜，关员在单据上盖章
scene: 跨境的货柜在港口堆了整排，报关员抱着单据来回奔走。The customs officer opened the crate and asked for the invoice.
sceneCN: 这里 customs 是「海关」（第 1 个义项：监管进出境货物并征税的政府机构）；句意：海关关员打开板条箱并要求出示发票。

derivatives.zh: 惯常的；按惯例的，由 custom 加形容词后缀 -ary 构成
习俗；惯例，customs 的单数形式，与「海关」义同源
顾客，由「惯常光顾」的 custom 义引申
海关大楼；税关，custom 与 house 的复合词

senses.title: The agency that controls goods at the border
senses.definition: the government department that inspects goods and collects duties when they enter or leave a country
senses.definitionCN: 在货物进出境时查验货物并征收关税的政府部门
senses.example: Customs held the container at the port for a full inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 海关把货柜扣在港口做全面查验。
senses.why: Medieval tolls were called customary dues, and the office that collected them took over the plural name.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的通行税被称为「惯常缴纳的款项」，征收它的机构就沿用了这个复数名称。

senses.title: The tax charged on imported goods
senses.definition: a tax that must be paid on goods brought into a country
senses.definitionCN: 对输入本国的货物所征的税
senses.example: The importer paid customs on the imported machinery.
senses.exampleCN: 进口商为进口机械缴纳了关税。
senses.why: The same plural word names both the office and the payment it collects, a common transfer from institution to charge.
senses.whyCN: 同一个复数词既指机构又指它征收的款项，这是从机构名转到费用的常见引申。

senses.title: The border point where goods are checked
senses.definition: the place at a port, airport, or border where goods and baggage are examined
senses.definitionCN: 港口、机场或边境上查验货物与行李的地点
senses.example: Please declare the samples at customs before your flight.
senses.exampleCN: 登机前请在海关申报这些样品。
senses.why: Because the agency works at fixed points, its name also labels the checkpoint itself.
senses.whyCN: 由于海关在固定地点办公，它的名称也被用来指那个检查地点本身。

intro.en: Customs comes from Latin consuetudo, habit, whose plural consuetudines named the customary dues paid on goods.
intro.cn: customs 来自拉丁语 consuetudo（习惯），其复数 consuetudines 指对货物惯常征收的款项。

items.en: Consuetudo means habit or established practice.
items.cn: consuetudo 意为习惯或既定惯例。

items.en: The plural consuetudines names customary payments and tolls.
items.cn: 复数 consuetudines 指按惯例缴纳的款项与通行税。

items.en: Costume means custom and also a customary toll.
items.cn: 古法语 costume 既指习俗，也指惯常征收的通行税。

items.en: English customs first names the customary tolls on goods.
items.cn: 英语 customs 最初指对货物按惯例征收的税。

items.en: Customs also comes to mean the office that collects the tolls.
items.cn: customs 又进而指征收这些税的机构。

items.en: Modern usage keeps customs for both the tax and the border agency.
items.cn: 现代用法让 customs 同时保留「关税」与「海关机构」两个意思。

note.en: Customs belongs to the custom family, and its closest tax neighbours are tariff, duty, and excise.
note.cn: customs 属于 custom 词族，最贴近的税种同类词是 tariff、duty 与 excise。

entries.definition: a habitual practice of a group or place
a person who buys goods from a shop
entries.definitionCN: 顾客；由「惯常光顾」引申，与海关义无关

entries.definition: a tax on goods entering or leaving a country
a tax paid on goods entering a country
a tax on goods made or sold inside a country

normalIntro.en: Customs began as customary payments, so the word ties habit to the tax table.
normalIntro.cn: customs 最初指按惯例缴纳的款项，这个词把「习惯」和税表系在一起。

normal.en: Latin consuetudo means habit, and customary dues took its plural.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 consuetudo 意为习惯，惯常缴纳的税项用了它的复数。

normal.en: Customs is plural in form and can take a singular or a plural verb.
normal.cn: customs 形式上是复数，动词可单可复。

normal.en: Customs duty is the tax, customs officer is the person.
normal.cn: customs duty 是税，customs officer 是人。

normal.en: Goods are cleared through customs before they enter the market.
normal.cn: 货物进入市场前要经海关结关。

normal.en: Compare custom and customs: one is a habit, the other is the border agency.
normal.cn: 对比 custom 与 customs：前者是习俗，后者是边境机构。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger of old tolls kept in a border tower.
abstract.cn: 想象边境塔楼里一本记着旧通行税的账簿。

abstract.en: Imagine a stamp coming down on a customs form.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章落在报关单上。

abstract.en: Think of a gate where every truck must stop and show papers.
abstract.cn: 想象一道大门，每辆卡车都得停下出示单据。

examples.en: Customs seized the shipment because the papers were false.
examples.cn: 海关查扣了这批货，因为单据是伪造的。

examples.en: The firm paid customs on every machine it imported last year.
examples.cn: 这家公司为去年进口的每台机器都缴了关税。

examples.en: The goods were cleared through customs at the inland depot.
examples.cn: 货物在内陆场站办结了海关手续。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡斯特姆斯」——谐音像「卡住货的税关」，货物进出都要被卡一下；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 consuetudo（习惯，源自 consuescere「使习惯」）→ 晚期拉丁语复数 consuetudines（按惯例缴纳的款项）→ 古法语 costume（惯例；通行税）→ 英语 custom 与 customs：由「惯例」转为「按惯例征收的关税」，再指征收它的海关。

sensesIntro.en: Customs first names the border agency, then the tax that agency collects, and finally the checkpoint where the work is done.
sensesIntro.cn: customs 先指边境机构，再指该机构征收的税，最后指办理这些手续的关卡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a border gate where every load is stopped and stamped.
core.cn: 核心意象：边境关口，每一车货都要停下盖章。

branches.en: The government body that inspects goods.
The place where goods are examined.
The agency is named by the charge it collects, so office and tax share one plural word.
branches.cn: 机构因它征收的款项得名，所以机构与税共用一个复数词。

branches.en: The agency works at fixed points, so its name also labels the gate.
branches.cn: 机构在固定地点办公，所以它的名称也指那道关口。

intro.en: Customs grows from the Latin noun consuetudo, habit, through the idea of dues paid by custom to the modern border agency.
intro.cn: customs 从拉丁语名词 consuetudo（习惯）出发，经「按惯例缴纳的款项」这一层，走到现代的边境机构。

latinIntro.en: Latin consuetudo means habit, and its plural consuetudines means customary payments.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 consuetudo 意为习惯，其复数 consuetudines 意为按惯例缴纳的款项。

items.example: Consuetudo is the noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: consuetudo 是整个词族背后的名词。

items.example: Consuescere is the verb that yields the noun.
items.exampleCN: consuescere 是产出这个名词的动词。

items.meaningCN: 惯常缴纳的款项与通行税
items.example: The plural name passes into English as customs.
items.exampleCN: 这个复数名称进入英语后成为 customs。

items.example: Costume carries both senses into French.
items.exampleCN: costume 把两个意思带入法语。

items.example: Custom keeps the habit sense.
items.exampleCN: custom 保留「习惯」义。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ary 构成这个形容词。

items.meaning: the border agency and its tax
items.example: Customs keeps both the office and the charge.
items.exampleCN: customs 同时保留机构与费用两个意思。

items.example: Customer grows from the idea of customary patronage.
items.exampleCN: customer 由「惯常光顾」的意思长出来。

items.example: The compound names the charge precisely.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词精确指出那笔费用。

items.meaning: a group of states with one tariff wall
items.example: The compound names a trade arrangement.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指一种贸易安排。
